title: Storybook
description: A children's picture book that tells only the story's key points: a cover, one page per key point — each page one big emoji scene over one short, friendly sentence — and a last page. The words get simpler and warmer; the facts stay exactly as the article gives them.

hero.description: The cover's hero emoji: the story's main character or thing, drawn very big.

friends.description: Optional: at most two more emoji placed beside the hero, and only ones that picture this beat (the sea under a boat, a question mark over a mystery). Decoration for its own sake is noise; leave the array out when the hero says it alone.

opening.description: The cover line, short and storybook-warm: who the story is about and where it happens, as the article gives them. Start it like a story ('Once upon a time, …').

pages.description: One page per KEY point of the story, in story order — usually two or three. First decide which few facts the story is actually about; supporting detail (ages, prices, names that carry nothing) stays out, even when it is interesting.

hero.description: This page's hero emoji, drawn very big: the thing this key point is about.

friends.description: Optional: at most two more emoji placed beside the hero, and only ones that picture this beat (the sea under a boat, a question mark over a mystery). Decoration for its own sake is noise; leave the array out when the hero says it alone.

text.description: ONE short, friendly sentence a child could follow, carrying one key point from the article, numbers copied exactly: "For 32 years, Petal splish-splashed across the river."

closing.description: Optional: the last page's line — what happens next, or a question for the reader. The template adds 'And so' in front of it, so start with a small letter.
